Utterance: Hi there, Ms. Stone? I'm BJ Daniel. Let me just wash my hands.
Just call me Dorothy.
The nurse mentioned you wanted to talk about your care. What's going on?
Five days ago I was in emergency and they put a tube down my throat. I tried to tell them I didn't want it. I hope it never happens again.
I understand that's scary. I've looked at your chart, but did anyone explain why they did it?
Not really, I was gasping for air. I'm really worried and I don't want that tube anymore. I'm okay to pass as I am.
We will respect your wishes. What is your understanding of what brought you here?
Congestive heart failure. There was water in my lungs, and the ambulance brought me in.
So they put the tube down quickly. Did anyone ask if you were okay with that?
I tried to gesture that I didn't want it. I've had it three times and don't want it again.
Do you know why they would have put the tube down?
I guess because I was short of air. They tried to save me.
Usually, we only use a tube as a last resort to save you. It suggests you were close to dying when you arrived.
I guess so, but I'm okay with dying. I've lived a good life. If the Good Lord says it's my time, I'm okay with that. Just no tube.
I hear you. For you, quality of life is more important than quantity. Is that correct?
That is correct. How can I be assured my wishes are respected?
I'll document this in your chart and create a 'Goals of Care' form. I'll also notify your family doctor and update the provincial emergency system.
Thank you. I was so concerned about that. It was a horrendous experience.
I need to ask a few routine questions. How is your mood?
I'm feeling fine. My mood is fine.
And how were you feeling about life before you came into the hospital?
I am enjoying life to the best I can.
Are you willing to have medications for your breathing, just not the intubation?
Certainly. Medication is fine, just not intubation.
If you were to pass away, would you want chest compressions or shocks to bring you back?
No. The Good Lord knows when it's my time.
What about BiPAP? It's a mask that pushes air in. It's a bit uncomfortable but not like the tube.
Would it be for a long time?
Usually only two to six hours. Also, would you be okay with the ICU for close monitoring without a tube?
Yes, I would be okay with that. It doesn't sound as invasive.
Summarizing: medicines and the mask are okay, but no breathing tube and no restarting your heart. Anything else?
No, I just needed to be reassured. I'm glad it's on my chart.
You can change your mind anytime, but this is the plan for now. I just want you to be aware of that.
Okay. I don't think I'll change my mind, but I'll talk to you if I do.
Let's go through some routine history. Heart failure, and anything else?
That's it, though there was something else starting with an S. I have a list of my medications here.
You're on Furosemide and Diltiazem. Any allergies? And you're 70, correct?
That's correct. I don't smoke, drink, or use street drugs or herbals.
Whereabouts are you living right now?
I moved to a convalescent home six months ago. I'd prefer my own home, but I'm learning to adjust.
I think I have all the information I need. Is there anything else you wanted to talk about?
No, you've answered my question. I was so worried about that tube.
It was very nice to meet you, Ms. Stone. See you later.
